_doc: Narration of the recorded demo, told as the story of the incident. `text` is the subtitle; `say` (optional) is what the voice reads when it should differ (numbers, times, acronyms). Avoid phrases like 'in Italian': the TTS model may take them as an instruction and switch language (tts.js verifies every line with a transcription and regenerates on mismatch). `who` and `shows` are retained in caption metadata. session.js refers to lines by `id` and waits for each line to finish before the next.

lines.text: Valverde valley, one in the afternoon. A wildfire has broken out on Pine Hill, and a strong north-east wind is pushing it towards the village of Pineta.
lines.shows: The situation: one device plays every role

lines.text: Four people run the response: the exercise director, the mayor of Valverde, the fire commander, and a regional civil protection officer who works in Armenian.
lines.shows: Each player works in their own language

lines.text: The exercise begins. The fire already covers five hectares and is spreading south-west through dry pine forest.
lines.shows: Turn-based control; turn speed set to 120×

lines.text: The first reports come in: emergency calls about the fire, a warning that the primary school is in session, and a fire-behaviour estimate for the commander.
lines.shows: Injects from the exercise script, translated for each player

lines.text: In Pineta, 120 pupils and staff are still inside the primary school, and the school has no transport of its own.
lines.say: In Pineta, one hundred and twenty pupils and staff are still inside the primary school, and the school has no transport of its own.
lines.shows: Role-specific information

lines.text: The mayor acts at once: warn the village, evacuate the school to the sports centre in Valverde, and close the northern road.
lines.shows: Free-text orders, no command language

lines.text: The fire commander sends ground crews to cut fire breaks north and east of the village, and an air tanker to wet the forest above it.
lines.shows: Orders by map zone and place name

lines.text: Before anything happens on the ground, every order is checked against the people, vehicles and authority actually available.
lines.shows: The AI interprets; the rules decide what is possible

lines.text: A problem emerges: evacuating the school needs 3 buses, and the town has only 2.
lines.say: A problem emerges: evacuating the school needs three buses, and the town has only two.
lines.shows: A real constraint the AI cannot wave away

lines.text: Exercise control steps in: the regional transport company can release one more bus.
lines.shows: The Director steers the scenario in plain language

lines.text: The extra bus is confirmed, and the mayor is told it is on its way.
lines.shows: Nothing changes until the Director approves

lines.text: The fire commander's plan goes ahead: two fire breaks and a water drop.
lines.shows: Approval, with a note to the player

lines.text: With three buses available, the school evacuation can start, together with a warning to the whole village.
lines.shows: Feasibility re-checked at the moment of decision

lines.text: The mayor receives the confirmation, and the buses head for the school.
lines.shows: Feedback in the player's language

lines.text: The next thirty minutes unfold. The fire runs downhill towards Pineta while the crews race to finish the breaks.
lines.shows: The turn is simulated live

lines.text: The tallest flames mark where the fire burns hottest and where most simulated runs agree. The faint glow ahead shows where it could spread next.
lines.shows: Flames from fire intensity and the Monte Carlo probability

lines.text: The fire breaks hold at the edge of the village, and the children reach the sports centre safely. The northern road is lost to the flames.
lines.shows: Consequences of the decisions

lines.text: Each responder receives a report on what has changed on the ground.
lines.shows: Situation updates for every role

lines.text: Half past one. The wind strengthens to 55 kilometres per hour, and a second fire starts in the farmland south-east of Pineta.
lines.say: Half past one. The wind strengthens to fifty-five kilometres per hour, and a second fire starts in the farmland south-east of Pineta.
lines.shows: Escalation by the Director

lines.text: Local resources are stretched. Regional civil protection asks for international help: two water-bombing aircraft through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism, and two more ground crews.
lines.say: Local resources are stretched. Regional civil protection asks for international help: two water-bombing aircraft through the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism, and two more ground crews.
lines.shows: International assistance (UCPM)

lines.text: Under pressure, the fire commander sends an unclear order…
…and is asked exactly where the crews should go, instead of anyone guessing.
lines.say: and is asked exactly where the crews should go, instead of anyone guessing.
lines.shows: Ambiguity is clarified, never guessed

lines.text: The answer comes back: the eastern edge of the village, and the slope above it.
lines.shows: The follow-up is read in context

lines.text: The request for aircraft and the new fire breaks are approved; the unclear order is sent back.
lines.shows: Every action passes through the Director

lines.text: The next hour. Reinforcements arrive and the breaks keep the fire out of Pineta, but the second fire races through the farmland, where nobody was warned.
lines.shows: The escalation, simulated live

lines.text: By half past two, Pineta is safe and every child is accounted for, but farmhouses have burned and the aircraft are still on their way. Every decision and its consequences are recorded for the debrief.
lines.shows: Outcome and debrief
